text.p: An earthquake measuring 4.2 on the Richter scale struck Nepal early on Tuesday, but there were no reports of injuries or damage, officials said.
The National Seismological Centre (NSC) said the epicentre was located near rural Rasuwa district, about 100 kilometres (60 miles) north of the capital Kathmandu.
NSC said the tremor hit at 1:51 a.m. (2006 GMT Monday).
Earthquakes measuring between four and five on the open-ended Richter scale are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in populated areas.
On Feb 1, Nepal's Kathmandu valley was rocked by two earthquakes and several tremors, but there were no casualties.
Two days later, two aftershocks rolled through the Kathmandu valley and kept fearful residents outside their homes, but no casualties were reported.
More than 700 people were killed when an earthquake measuring 6.5 on the Richter scale hit Udayapur in eastern Nepal in 1988.
